relations.subject: server:node-recovery
relations.evidence: The recovery command also allows a server to have it's data removed before being added back to the cluster (full recovery) or having the server resume from where it last left off (delta recovery).

relations.subject: server:delta-recovery
relations.evidence: Delta recovery will always take the least amount of time and is the recommended recovery mode.

relations.subject: server:full-recovery
relations.evidence: To specify full recovery set this option to "full". For delta recovery set this option to "delta". The default value for this option is "full".

relations.subject: server:rebalance
relations.evidence: Note that after the recovery subcommand is run you must rebalance the cluster. See the [rebalance](couchbase-cli-rebalance.md) command for more information on rebalancing a cluster.

notable_absence.finding: As with every other file in this batch, no specific RBAC role or privilege is named for the recovery subcommand - only the generic 'unauthorized error' boilerplate.

cross_component_finding: A genuine internal inconsistency: the DESCRIPTION states 'Delta recovery will always take the least amount of time and is the recommended recovery mode,' yet the --recovery-type OPTIONS text states the flag's default is 'full' ('The default value for this option is "full".'). The CLI's own default contradicts its own stated recommendation - a reader who omits --recovery-type gets the mode the page itself calls non-recommended. This is exactly the kind of docs-issue-shaped inconsistency the round's authorship-provenance hypothesis predicts from lighter TW review (an engineer wrote the accurate default-value fact and the recommendation-framing sentence in the same page without reconciling them). Otherwise terminology ('delta recovery', 'full recovery') matches the promoted registry cleanly.
cross_product_finding: Not addressed on this page - no comparison to Capella, which manages node recovery internally with no customer-facing CLI equivalent to full/delta recovery mode selection.
